native_result.query: In which millenium did amber had the highest value and in what time interval did it peak?
native_result.HypoA: Amber has historically high and stable values in the 4th millenium BCE. with its all time peak around 3300 to 3000BCE.
native_result.HypoB: Amber reached its highest relative importance (used here as a proxy: standardised find-abundance Z values; the data contain no price/value field, so frequency is not literally value) in the 4th millennium BCE, 4000-3001 BCE (CE -4000..-3001 = 4951-5950 calBP): the mean of the interpolated amber Z series is +1.488 for that millennium versus -0.277 (3000-2001 BCE) and -0.556 (2000-1001 BCE), a 1.77 SD gap. Within it the curve forms two plateaux (Z=+1.46 over 4000-3401 BCE and the series maximum Z=+1.54 over 3300-2901 BCE), so amber peaked in the interval ~3400-3000 BCE, best stated as the century-bin core 3300-2901 BCE (5250-4851 calBP) inside a broader high stand of 4000-2901 BCE (5950-4851 calBP), with +/-100 y (one century-bin) uncertainty and no resolvable sub-century ordering. In period terms the maximum coincides with the Middle Neolithic (mean Z +1.524, all 5 bins in the peak) after an Early Neolithic rise at 4000 BCE and before a collapse from 2900 BCE (SG -0.223, LN -0.880). Relative to the Belau single-site openness proxy the amber maximum is much earlier (smoothed amber peak 3275-3175 BCE vs pollen maximum at the 704 BCE record edge) and the two series are negatively correlated at all lags (r(0) = -0.43), i.e. amber, as a form of social capital, is most prominent while land-use/openness was still low.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Audit script verified alignment (CE = -BCE; calBP = 1950 - CE exact in both yearly files; no duplicate years or gaps; Amber == Zamber on 37 anchors, Amber_inter == linear interpolation, max dev 2e-16; 100-y binned anchors on a yearly grid). 2) Built century-bin table with period labels plus bin means of Amber_inter and 100/250/500 y centred rolling means. 3) Primary criterion R1: interval mean of Amber_inter per millennium (astronomical and data-anchored boundaries; blocks with <80% coverage excluded but reported) plus a sliding 1000-y window scan for boundary-phase robustness. 4) Peak interval by three determinations: M1 longest contiguous set of century bins >= threshold (mean+1SD, top decile, half-max), M2 highest-value anchor platform, M3 smoothed-peak neighbourhood (50/100/250/500 y), with continuous interpolated crossings shown as reference only. 5) Sensitivity over bin width 100-1200 y, three thresholds, four smoothing windows, 37 vs 39 bins, raw anchors vs interpolation. 6) Interpretive lead-lag/cross-correlation against ts.pollen_inter_100 (Belau single site; forward-fill artefact beyond CE -704 flagged; pollen_grate_100 excluded). All rules were fixed before execution and every statement carries +/-100 y plus the frequency-is-not-value caveat.
